   900	\label{sec:qld-game}
   901	
   902	We start by discussing parameter settings.
   903	The game $\game^\pauli$ is parametrized by a tuple
   904	\[\qldparams = (q,m,d)\;,\] where $q,m,d \in \N$ are integers. 
   905	We sometimes write $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$ to emphasize the dependence of the
   906	Pauli basis test on the parameters.
   907	
   908	Informally, the test is meant to certify that the players share a state of the
   909	form $\ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes M}$, where $M=2^m$.
   910	Its question set includes questions that are axis-parallel/diagonal lines and points in $\F_q^m$,
   911	which are meant to correspond to questions in the classical low-degree test, and questions
   912	of the form $(\Pauli, W)$, for $W \in \{X, Z\}$.
   913	Upon receipt of a question of the latter form, the players are expected to
   914	perform the POVM $\{\tau_h^W\}_{h \in \F_q^{M}}$ and report the outcome $h$ as
   915	their answer.
   916	
   917	The key idea behind the test
   918	is for the provers to encode their outcomes using the \emph{low-degree encoding} from Section~\ref{sec:ld-encoding}.
   919	Given an outcome $h \in \F_q^M$, the low-degree encoding of~$h$ is the polynomial $g_h:\F_q^m \rightarrow \F_q$.
   920	Rather than asking the provers to always return the entire string~$h$,
   921	many of the subtests in the game $\game^\pauli$ will ``probe'' limited information about~$h$ as follows:
   922	the verifier provides the provers with a string $u_W \in \F_q^m$,
   923	and using this they are expected to evaluate $g_h(u_W) \in \F_q$ and return it to the verifier.
   924	For a fixed value of~$W$, then, the prover's responses to these ``probes'' should be consistent with some low-degree polynomial in the input~$u_W$.
   925	To check this, the verifier can perform the classical low-degree test from Section~\ref{sec:ld-verifier}.
   926	This ensures that the prover's responses for the $W = X$ basis are consistent with each other,
   927	as well as their responses for the $W = Z$ basis, although it does not test consistency between the $X$ and $Z$ responses.
   928	
   929	The next set of subtests the verifier performs ensure that the provers' $X$ and $Z$ measurements are consistent with each other.
   930	On the $X$ side, consider the measurement in which the prover performs the $\{\tau_h^X\}$ POVM,
   931	receives outcome $h_X$, and outputs $g_{h_X}(u_X) \in \F_q$.
   932	For technical reasons that will become clear shortly,
   933	it will be convenient for the prover's measurement to have two outcomes rather than~$q$ outcomes.
   934	To accomplish this, the verifier also provides the prover with an element $r_X \in \F_q$;
   935	given this, the prover should output not $g_{h_X}(u_X) \in \F_q$ but $\tr(g_{h_X}(u_X) \cdot r_X)$, which is an element of $\F_2$.
   936	Similarly, on the $Z$ side, suppose the prover is provided $r_Z \in \F_q$,
   937	performs $\{\tau_h^Z\}$ to receive $h_Z$, and outputs $\tr(g_{h_Z}(u_Z) \cdot r_Z) \in \F_2$.
   938	Together, these two are a pair of two-outcome measurements, one in the~$X$ basis and one in the~$Z$ basis,
   939	and as it turns out, this pair of measurements either commutes with each other or anticommutes with each other
   940	(this is why we modified the measurements to have only two outcomes).
   941	The key quantity to determine which of these is the case is the following complicated-looking expression:
   942	\begin{equation*}
   943	\gamma = \tr \bigl( (\ind_{m}(u_\xpt) \cdot r_\xpt) \cdot
   944	      (\ind_{m}(u_\zpt) \cdot r_\zpt) \bigr)\;.
   945	\end{equation*}
   946	If $\gamma = 0$, then these two measurements commute, and if $\gamma = 1$, then these two measurements anticommute
   947	(this fact is established in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:pauli-completeness} below).
   948	In the $\gamma = 0$ case, the verifier can check whether these two measurements commute by performing the ``commutation check'',
   949	which asks the provers to simultaneously measure both $\tr(g_{h_X}(u_X) \cdot r_X)$ and $\tr(g_{h_Z}(u_Z) \cdot r_Z)$ and report their values.
   950	In the $\gamma = 1$ case, on the other hand, the measurements anticommute, which implies that they cannot simultaneously be measured.
   951	In spite of this, the verifier can still check that the measurements anticommute by using the Magic Square game from Section~\ref{sec:ms} above.
   952	As was shown in Theorem~\ref{thm:ms-from-ac}, any pair of anticommuting measurements
   953	can be used to form a perfect strategy for the Magic Square game
   954	(and indeed the reverse is true as well: any perfect strategy for the Magic Square game entails a pair of anticommuting measurements).
   955	
   956	Together, these give the main subtests for the game $\game^\pauli$.
   957	
   958	\begin{definition}[Admissible parameters]\label{def:admissible}
   959	  We say that the tuple $\qldparams=(q, m, d)$ is \emph{admissible} if $q$ is
   960	  an admissible field size (Definition~\ref{def:admissible-size}) and $m | q$.
   961	\end{definition}
   962	
   963	
   964	\paragraph{Question distribution.}
   965	We now describe the question distribution of the game $\game^\pauli$, and show
   966	that it is a (typed) CL distribution.
   967	The question types in the game $\game^\pauli$ are
   968	\begin{equation}
   969	  \label{eq:pauli-type}
   970	  \type^\pauli= \bigl( \{\Point, \ALine, \DLine, \Pauli, \Pair \} \times \{X,Z\} \bigr)
   971	  \cup \type^\ms \cup \{\Pair\}\;,
   972	\end{equation}
   973	where $\type^\ms$ is the question type set of the Magic Square game defined in
   974	Section~\ref{sec:ms}.
   975	
   976	
   977	
   978	
   979	Before presenting the CL functions of the Pauli basis test, we first give an
   980	intuitive description of the question distribution of the Pauli basis test: a
   981	pair of questions $((\tvar_\alice, x_\alice), (\tvar_\bob, x_\bob))$ in
   982	$\game^\pauli$ can be sampled via the following procedure:
   983	
   984	\begin{enumerate}
   985	\item Sample a pair of types by sampling an edge $(\tvar_\alice, \tvar_\bob)$ of
   986	  the graph $G^\pauli$ given in Figure~\ref{fig:type-graph-pauli} uniformly at
   987	  random (including the self-loops).
   988	\item Sample the following uniformly at random:
   989		\begin{enumerate}
   990		\item (\emph{Points}) $u_\xpt,u_\zpt \in \F_q^m$,
   991		\item (\emph{Directions}) $s \in \F_q$, $v \in \F_q^m$,
   992	  \item (\emph{Qubit basis for (anti-)commutation}) $r_\xpt,r_\zpt \in \F_q$.
   993		\end{enumerate}
   994	\item For $w \in \AB$ and $W\in\{X,Z\}$,
   995		\begin{enumerate}
   996	  \item If $\tvar_w = (\Point, W)$, then set $x_w = u_W$,
   997	  \item If $\tvar_w = (\ALine, W)$, then set $x_w = (u_0,s)$, where $u_0 =
   998	    L^\lnf_{e_i}(u_W)$, with $i = \chi(s)$ (see \Cref{sec:ld-game} for
   999	    definition of $L^\lnf$ and $\chi(s)$),
  1000	  \item If $\tvar_w = (\DLine,W)$, then set $x_w = (u_0,s,v')$, where $i =
  1001	    \chi(s)$, $v' = \pi_{i-1}(v)$, and $u_0 = L^\lnf_{v'}(u_W)$,
  1002	  \item If $\tvar_w = \Constraint_i$ for some $i\in\{1,\ldots,6\}$, then set
  1003	    $x_w = (u_\xpt, u_\zpt, r_\xpt, r_\zpt)$,
  1004	  \item If $\tvar_w = \Variable_j$ for some $j\in\{1,\ldots,9\}$, then set $x_w
  1005	    = (u_\xpt, u_\zpt, r_\xpt, r_\zpt)$,
  1006	  \item If $\tvar_w = \Pair$, then set $x_w = (u_\xpt, u_\zpt, r_\xpt, r_\zpt)$,
  1007	  \item If $\tvar_w = (\Pair, W)$, then set $x_w = (u_\xpt, u_\zpt, r_\xpt, r_\zpt)$,
  1008	  \item If $\tvar_w = (\Pauli, W)$, then set $x_w = 0$.
  1009		\end{enumerate}
  1010	\end{enumerate}

  1072	
  1073	\paragraph{Conditional linear functions for the Pauli basis test.}
  1074	The CL functions corresponding to the Pauli basis test question distribution are
  1075	parameterized by the parameter tuple $\qldparams = (q,m,d)$.
  1076	Let $V^\pauli$ denote the linear space $(\F_q^m)^2 \times \F_q \times \F_q^m
  1077	\times (\F_q)^2$.
  1078	The space $V^\pauli$ is decomposed into a direct sum of the following register
  1079	subspaces: $V_\xpt,V_\zpt$ (which are $m$-dimensional), $V_\coord$ (which is
  1080	$1$-dimensional), $V_{\dir{}}$ (which is $m$-dimensional), and
  1081	$V_{\rxpt},V_{\rzpt}$ (which are $1$-dimensional).
  1082	We identify elements of $V^\pauli$ as tuples $(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1083	\in (\F_q^m)^2 \times \F_q \times \F_q^m \times (\F_q)^2$.
  1084	We define CL functions $L_\tvar: V^\pauli \to V^\pauli$ for every type $\tvar
  1085	\in \type^\pauli$:
  1086	\begin{enumerate}
  1087	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\Point,W}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1088	  = L_\Point(u_W,s,v)$ where $L_\Point$ is the $1$-level CL function defined in
  1089	  \Cref{eq:cl-ptf}.\footnote{The range $V_{\xpt} \oplus V_\coord \oplus
  1090	    V_{\dir{}}$ or $V_{\zpt} \oplus V_\coord \oplus V_{\dir{}}$ of $L_\Point$ is
  1091	    embedded in $V^\pauli$ in the natural way.
  1092	    The same convention is used also in Item 2 and 3 for $L_\ALine$ and
  1093	    $L_\DLine$.}
  1094	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\ALine,W}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1095	  = L_\ALine(u_W,s,v)$ where $L_\ALine$ is the $2$-level CL function defined in
  1096	  \Cref{eq:cl-alnf}.
  1097	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\DLine,W}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1098	  = L_\DLine(u_W,s,v)$ where $L_\DLine$ is the $3$-level CL function defined in
  1099	  \Cref{eq:cl-dlnf}.
  1100	\item For $\tvar \in \type^\ms \cup \{\Pair, (\Pair,X), (\Pair,Z) \}$,
  1101	  $L_{\tvar}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt) =
  1102	  (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,0,0,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)$, i.e., it projects onto $V_\xpt \oplus
  1103	  V_\zpt \oplus V_{\rxpt} \oplus V_{\rzpt}$.
  1104	  Thus $L_{\tvar}$ is a $1$-level CL function.
  1105	  
  1106	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\Pauli,W} = 0$ as the identically $0$
  1107	  function.
  1108	  Thus it is a $0$-level CL function.
  1109	
  1110	\end{enumerate}
  1111	We note that the maps $L_{\Point,W}, L_{\ALine,W}, L_{\DLine,W}$ act as the zero function
  1112	on $V_{\overline{W}} \oplus V_{\rxpt} \oplus V_{\rzpt}$ where $\overline{W} = X$
  1113	if $W = Z$ and $\overline{W} = Z$ if $W = X$.
  1114	
  1115	The question distribution of $\game^\pauli$ is thus a typed CL distribution on
  1116	$\type^\pauli \times V^\pauli \times \type^\pauli \times V^\pauli$ where
  1117	$(\tvar_\alice,x_\alice,\tvar_\bob,x_\bob)$ is sampled by first uniformly
  1118	sampling an edge $(\tvar_\alice,\tvar_\bob)$ from the graph $G^\pauli$ defined
  1119	in Figure~\ref{fig:type-graph-pauli}, sampling a uniformly random $z \in
  1120	V^\pauli$, and then setting $x_w = L_{\tvar_w}(z)$ for $w \in \AB$.

275	We note that the marginal functions, factor spaces, and linear maps of a given
   276	CL function $L$ may not be unique; for example, consider the identity function
   277	on a linear space $V = \F^n$.
   278	This is clearly a $1$-level CL function, but it can also be viewed as a
   279	$k$-level CL function for $k \in \{2, \ldots, n\}$ with an arbitrary partition
   280	of $V$ into factor spaces.
   281	
   282	\begin{lemma}
   283	  \label{lem:cl-concat}
   284	  Let $\ell, k \ge 0$ be integers and $U = \F^n$, $V = \F^m$ be linear spaces.
   285	  Suppose $L$ is a $k$-level CL function on $U$ and $R_u$ is an $\ell$-level CL
   286	  function on $V$ for each $u \in L(U)$.
   287	  Then the \emph{concatenation} $T$ of $L$ and $\{R_u\}_u$ defined as
   288	  \begin{equation*}
   289	    T (x) = L(x^U) + R_{L(x^U)} (x^V)
   290	  \end{equation*}
   291	  is a $(k+\ell)$-level conditionally linear function on $U\oplus V$.
   292	\end{lemma}
   293	
   294	\begin{proof}
   295	  We prove the claim by induction on $k$.
   296	  The case $k = 0$ follows from the Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}.
   297	  Assume that the lemma holds for $L$ being at most $(k-1)$-level.
   298	  By Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}, there are complementary register subspaces
   299	  $U_1$ and $U_{>1}$ of $U$, a linear function $L_1$ on $U_1$, and a family of
   300	  $(k-1)$-level CL functions $L_{>1,\, v}$ for $v \in L_1(U_1)$ such that
   301	  \begin{equation*}
   302	    L(x^U) = x^{L_1} + L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1}}).
   303	  \end{equation*}
   304	  For all $x^{L_1}$, define the function $T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ on $U_{>1} \oplus V$ as
   305	  \begin{equation*}
   306	    T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1} \oplus V}) = L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1}}) +
   307	    R_{x^{L_1} + x^{L_{>1}}}(x^V),
   308	  \end{equation*}
   309	  the concatenation of $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ and $\{ R_{L(x^U)} \}_{x^{L_{>1}}}$
   310	  where $L_{>1}$ is the shorthand notation of $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$.
   311	  By the induction hypothesis, $T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ is $(k+\ell-1)$-level
   312	  conditionally linear.
   313	  The lemma follows from Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}.
   314	\end{proof}
   315	\begin{lemma}[Direct sums of CL functions]
   316	  \label{lem:cl-func-prod}
   317	  Let $V^{(1)}, V^{(2)}, \ldots, V^{(m)}$ be register subspaces of $V$ such that
   318	  $V = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}$.
   319	  Suppose that, for each $j\in\{1, 2, \ldots, m\}$, $L^{(j)}$ is an
   320	  $\ell_j$-level conditionally linear function on $V^{(j)}$.
   321	  Then the direct sum $L = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}$ is an $\ell$-level CL
   322	  function over $V$ for $\ell = \max_j \{\ell_j\}$, where $L$ is defined by
   323	  \begin{equation*}
   324	    L(x) = \sum_{j=1}^m  L^{(j)}(x^{(j)})
   325	  \end{equation*}
   326	  for all $x = \sum_{j=1}^m x^{(j)} \in \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}$.
   327	\end{lemma}
   328	
   329	\begin{proof}
   330	  It is easy to see that an $\ell$-level CL function is also $k$-level
   331	  conditionally linear for all $k \ge \ell$.
   332	  Hence, it suffices to prove the claim where $\ell_j = \ell$ for $j=1, 2,
   333	  \ldots, m$.
   334	
   335	  We prove the theorem by an induction on $\ell$.
   336	  For $\ell = 1$, the functions $L^{(j)}$ are linear and the claim follows by
   337	  the fact that the direct sum of linear maps is linear.
   338	
   339	  Assume now the theorem holds for conditionally linear functions of level at
   340	  most $\ell-1$ and $L^{(j)}$ are $\ell$-level conditionally linear functions
   341	  for $j=1, 2, ,\ldots, m$.
   342	  By definition, $L^{(j)}$ is the concatenation of conditionally linear
   343	  functions $L^{(j)}_{1}$ on $V^{(j)}_1$ and $\{ L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j} \}_{v_j}$
   344	  on $V^{(j)}_{>1}$ of levels $1$, and $\ell-1$ respectively.
   345	  Furthermore,
   346	  \begin{equation*}
   347	    L(x) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)} (x^{(j)}) = \sum_{j=1}^m \Bigl( v_j +
   348	    L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j}
   349	    \Bigl((x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_{>1}} \Bigr) \Bigr),
   350	  \end{equation*}
   351	  where $v_j = L^{(j)}_{1}\Bigl( (x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_1}
   352	    \Bigr)$.
   353	  By the induction hypothesis,
   354	  \begin{equation*}
   355	    L_{1} (x^{V_1}) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}_{1}\Bigl( (x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_1}
   356	    \Bigr),\quad L_{>1,\, v} (x^{V_{>1}}) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j}
   357	    \Bigl((x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_{>1}} \Bigr)
   358	  \end{equation*}
   359	  are $1$-level and $(\ell-1)$-level conditionally linear respectively for $v =
   360	  \sum_j v_j$, $V_1 = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}_1$, and $V_{>1} =
   361	  \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}_{>1}$.
   362	  This proves that $L$ is $\ell$-level conditionally linear.
   363	\end{proof}

   365	\begin{lemma}
   366	  \label{lem:cl-dist-prod}
   367	  For each $i \in \{1,\ldots,m\}$ let $L^{(i)}, R^{(i)} : V^{(i)} \to V^{(i)}$
   368	  be $\ell_i$-level conditionally linear functions and let $L, R: V \to V$ be the
   369	  direct sums $L = \bigoplus_i L_i$ and $R = \bigoplus_i R_i$, respectively, as
   370	  defined in Lemma~\ref{lem:cl-func-prod}.
   371	  Then the conditionally linear distribution $\mu_{L, R}$ is the product
   372	  distribution $\prod_{i=1}^m \mu_{L^{(i)},\, R^{(i)}}$ over $V \times V$.
   373	\end{lemma}
   374	
   375	\begin{proof}
   376		The distribution $\mu_{L,R}$ is the distribution over pairs $(L(x),R(x))$
   377	  where $x$ is sampled uniformly from $V \times V$.
   378	  By Lemma~\ref{lem:cl-func-prod}, this is equivalent to the distribution over
   379	  pairs $\bigl( (L_i(x^{V_i}))_{i=1}^m, (R_i(x^{V_i}))_{i=1}^m \bigr)$ where $x$
   380	  is chosen uniformly at random from $V$.
   381	  This distribution is exactly the product of the distributions $
   382	  \mu_{L^{(i)},\, R^{(i)}}$ for $i = 1, 2, \ldots, m$.
   383	\end{proof}

   102	\paragraph{Axis-parallel lines and diagonal lines.}
   103	Before presenting a formal description of the game $\game^\ld$, we first define
   104	what we mean by lines, and their properties.
   105	
   106	\begin{definition}[Lines]
   107	  \label{def:line}
   108		A \emph{line} $\line$ in $\F^m_q$ specified by a pair $(u,v) \in (\F_q^m)^2$
   109	  is the subset
   110	  \begin{equation}
   111	    \label{eq:line-set}
   112	    \line(u,v) = \bigl\{\, u + tv : t \in \F_q \,\bigr\} \subseteq \F_q^m \;.
   113	  \end{equation}
   114	  We call the vector $v$ a \emph{direction} of line
   115	  $\line(u,v)$.\footnote{For convenience we explicitly allow
   116	    $v=0$, in which case the line is reduced to a singleton.}
   117	  
   118	  A line $\line(u,v)$ is \emph{axis-parallel} if there is a coordinate $i \in
   119	  \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$ for which $v$ is equal to $e_i$, the $i$-th elementary basis
   120	  vector in $\F_q^m$.
   121	  We say that such a line $\line$ is \emph{parallel to the $i$-th direction}.
   122	  A line $\line(u,v)$ is \emph{diagonal} if there exists an $i \in
   123	  \{0,1,\ldots,m-1\}$ for which $v_1 = v_2 = \cdots = v_i = 0$.
   124	\end{definition}
   125	
   126	The following Proposition establishes that, for a fixed direction, a line
   127	$\line$ is an equivalence class of points on the line.
   128	\begin{proposition}
   129	  \label{prop:line-equiv}
   130	  Let $u,v \in \F_q^m$.
   131	  Then for all $u' \in \line(u,v)$, we have that $\line(u,v) = \line(u',v)$.
   132	\end{proposition}
   133	\begin{proof}
   134		Fix $u' \in \line(u,v)$.
   135	  We have that $u' = u + tv$ for some $t \in \F_q$.
   136	  Let $a \in \line(u,v)$.
   137	  This means that $a = u + sv$ for some $s\in \F_q$.
   138	  We also have that $a = u + (s - t + t)v = u + tv + (s - t)v = u' + (s - t)v$,
   139	  so $\line(u,v) \subseteq \line(u',v)$.
   140	  A similar argument shows that $\line(u',v) \subseteq \line(u,v)$.
   141	\end{proof}
   142	
   143	We now specify a canonical representation of lines $\line = \line(u,v)$ as pairs $(u_0,v)$
   144	where $u_0$ is a \emph{canonical representative} of $\line$ specified as
   145	follows.
   146	Let $L_v^{\lnf}: \F_q^m \to \F_q^m$ denote the canonical linear map with the
   147	one-dimensional kernel basis $\{v\}$ (see \Cref{def:cl-canonical} for a
   148	definition of canonical linear map).
   149	Note that for all $u \in \line$, we have that $L_v^{\lnf}(u)$ is a point in
   150	$\line$.
   151	This is because since the image and kernel of $L_v^{\lnf}$ are complementary
   152	subspaces by definition (see \Cref{def:cl-canonical}), any $u \in \F_q^m$ has a
   153	unique decomposition $u = u_0 + u_1$ where $u_0$ is in the image of $L_v^{\lnf}$
   154	and $u_1 \in \ker(L_v^{\lnf})$, which by definition is the subspace spanned by
   155	$v$.
   156	Thus $u_1 = tv$ for some $t \in \F_q$ and we have that $u_0 = u - tv \in \line$.
   157	In particular, if $u\in \line$ then $u_0 = L_v^{\lnf}(u) \in \line$ as well. 
   158	Furthermore, since $L_v^{\lnf}$ is a projection onto its image by definition, we
   159	have $L_v^{\lnf}(u_0) = u_0$.
   160	
   161	Next, note that for any $u,u' \in \line$, since $u-u' = sv$ for some $s\in \F_q$
   162	it follows that $L_v^\lnf(u) = L_v^\lnf(u')$.
   163	Thus $u_0 = u_0'$ and this shows that $L_v^\lnf$ gives a means to compute a
   164	canonical representative of lines.
   165	
   166	\begin{definition}[Canonical representative of a line]
   167	  \label{def:line-representative}
   168	  Let $\line$ be a line in direction $v$.
   169	  A canonical representative of $\line$ is the point $u_0 \in \F_q^m$ such that
   170	  \[
   171	    u_0 = L_v^\lnf(u)
   172	  \]
   173	  for all $u \in \line$.
   174	\end{definition}

   245		Consider the pair $(\line, u)$ sampled in the following way: first, sample the

   256	  Since $u_0 = L^{\lnf}_{e_i}(u)$, we have that $u \in \line(u_0,e_i)$.
   257	\end{proof}

  1073	\paragraph{Conditional linear functions for the Pauli basis test.}
  1074	The CL functions corresponding to the Pauli basis test question distribution are
  1075	parameterized by the parameter tuple $\qldparams = (q,m,d)$.
  1076	Let $V^\pauli$ denote the linear space $(\F_q^m)^2 \times \F_q \times \F_q^m
  1077	\times (\F_q)^2$.
  1078	The space $V^\pauli$ is decomposed into a direct sum of the following register
  1079	subspaces: $V_\xpt,V_\zpt$ (which are $m$-dimensional), $V_\coord$ (which is
  1080	$1$-dimensional), $V_{\dir{}}$ (which is $m$-dimensional), and
  1081	$V_{\rxpt},V_{\rzpt}$ (which are $1$-dimensional).
  1082	We identify elements of $V^\pauli$ as tuples $(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1083	\in (\F_q^m)^2 \times \F_q \times \F_q^m \times (\F_q)^2$.
  1084	We define CL functions $L_\tvar: V^\pauli \to V^\pauli$ for every type $\tvar
  1085	\in \type^\pauli$:
  1086	\begin{enumerate}
  1087	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\Point,W}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1088	  = L_\Point(u_W,s,v)$ where $L_\Point$ is the $1$-level CL function defined in
  1089	  \Cref{eq:cl-ptf}.\footnote{The range $V_{\xpt} \oplus V_\coord \oplus
  1090	    V_{\dir{}}$ or $V_{\zpt} \oplus V_\coord \oplus V_{\dir{}}$ of $L_\Point$ is
  1091	    embedded in $V^\pauli$ in the natural way.
  1092	    The same convention is used also in Item 2 and 3 for $L_\ALine$ and
  1093	    $L_\DLine$.}
  1094	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\ALine,W}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1095	  = L_\ALine(u_W,s,v)$ where $L_\ALine$ is the $2$-level CL function defined in
  1096	  \Cref{eq:cl-alnf}.
  1097	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\DLine,W}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1098	  = L_\DLine(u_W,s,v)$ where $L_\DLine$ is the $3$-level CL function defined in
  1099	  \Cref{eq:cl-dlnf}.
  1100	\item For $\tvar \in \type^\ms \cup \{\Pair, (\Pair,X), (\Pair,Z) \}$,
  1101	  $L_{\tvar}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt) =
  1102	  (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,0,0,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)$, i.e., it projects onto $V_\xpt \oplus
  1103	  V_\zpt \oplus V_{\rxpt} \oplus V_{\rzpt}$.
  1104	  Thus $L_{\tvar}$ is a $1$-level CL function.
  1105	  
  1106	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\Pauli,W} = 0$ as the identically $0$
  1107	  function.
  1108	  Thus it is a $0$-level CL function.
  1109	
  1110	\end{enumerate}
  1111	We note that the maps $L_{\Point,W}, L_{\ALine,W}, L_{\DLine,W}$ act as the zero function
  1112	on $V_{\overline{W}} \oplus V_{\rxpt} \oplus V_{\rzpt}$ where $\overline{W} = X$
  1113	if $W = Z$ and $\overline{W} = Z$ if $W = X$.
  1114	
  1115	The question distribution of $\game^\pauli$ is thus a typed CL distribution on
  1116	$\type^\pauli \times V^\pauli \times \type^\pauli \times V^\pauli$ where
  1117	$(\tvar_\alice,x_\alice,\tvar_\bob,x_\bob)$ is sampled by first uniformly
  1118	sampling an edge $(\tvar_\alice,\tvar_\bob)$ from the graph $G^\pauli$ defined
  1119	in Figure~\ref{fig:type-graph-pauli}, sampling a uniformly random $z \in
  1120	V^\pauli$, and then setting $x_w = L_{\tvar_w}(z)$ for $w \in \AB$.
  1121

    41	    [DecidableEq ι] : ℕ → Type _ where
    42	  | zero : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) 0
    43	  | succ {ell : ℕ}
    44	      (S₁ : Finset ι)
    45	      (L₁ : (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K))
    46	      (hSupport : ∀ x i, i ∉ S₁ → L₁ x i = 0)
    47	      (rest : (ι → K) → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell) :
    48	      CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) (ell + 1)

   311	def condLinearConcat {ιU ιV : Type*} [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU]
   312	    [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV] (L : (ιU → K) → (ιU → K))
   313	    (R : (ιU → K) → (ιV → K) → (ιV → K))
   314	    (x : ιU ⊕ ιV → K) : ιU ⊕ ιV → K :=
   315	  let u : ιU → K := fun i => x (.inl i)
   316	  let v : ιV → K := fun j => x (.inr j)

   325	theorem IsCondLinearOn.concat {ιU ιV : Type*} [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU]
   326	    [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV] {ell k : ℕ}
   327	    {L : (ιU → K) → (ιU → K)}
   328	    {R : (ιU → K) → (ιV → K) → (ιV → K)}
   329	    (hL : IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ : Finset ιU) k L)

   343	      exact (Classical.choose_spec (hR u hu)).1
   344	    · simp only [rTerm, dif_neg hu]

   348	    simp only [rTerm, dif_pos hu]

   357	          (Finset.univ : Finset (ιU ⊕ ιV)) := by
   358	      ext i
   359	      cases i <;> simp
   360	    simpa only [huniv] using hsupport

   362	    rw [CondLinearTerm.eval_concat]
   363	    simp only [zero_add]
   364	    rw [congrFun htL_eval (fun i => x (.inl i))]
   365	    rw [hr_eval (L (fun i => x (.inl i))) ⟨_, rfl⟩]

   396	    ⟨ldPointRegister_subset_sdiff_seed P, fun _ => trivial⟩⟩, ?_⟩
   397	  funext x
   398	  have hseed :

   400	        LdSpace.seed x := coordinateRestriction_seed P x
   401	  have hpoint : LdSpace.point (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x) =
   402	      LdSpace.point x := coordinateRestriction_point P x
   403	  have hval :
   404	      CondLinearTerm.eval (ldALineTerm P) x =
   405	        ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x) +

    21	/-- The admissibility predicate for a parameter tuple `(q, m, d)`. -/
    22	def IsAdmissibleTuple (t : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ) : Prop :=
    23	  IsAdmissibleSize t.1 ∧ 1 ≤ t.2.1 ∧ 1 ≤ t.2.2 ∧ t.2.1 ∣ t.1

    25	/-- Convert an admissible tuple to the parameter structure used by the
    26	Pauli basis game. -/
    27	def AdmissibleParams.ofTuple (t : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ)
    28	    (h : IsAdmissibleTuple t) : AdmissibleParams where
    29	  q := t.1
    30	  m := t.2.1

    36	/-- The smallest even natural number represented by the ceiling prescription
    37	in `def:introparams`. -/
    38	noncomputable def introParamsC (a b : ℝ) : ℕ :=
    39	  2 * ⌈(b + a) / (2 * b)⌉₊

    41	/-- The canonical `(q, m, d)` tuple of `def:introparams`. -/
    42	def introParamsTuple (c R : ℕ) : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ :=
    43	  (2 ^ (c * Nat.clog 2 (Nat.clog 2 R) + 1),
    44	    2 ^ Nat.log 2 (c * Nat.clog 2 R + 1), 1)
    45	
    46	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: a numerical comparison of the two exponents
    47	appearing in the canonical tuple.  If `s` is positive and `r` is at most
    48	`2 ^ s`, then the base-two logarithm of `c * r + 1` does not exceed
    49	`c * s + 1`. -/
    50	private theorem log_two_le_mul_add_one (c r s : ℕ) (hs : 1 ≤ s)
    51	    (hrs : r ≤ 2 ^ s) : Nat.log 2 (c * r + 1) ≤ c * s + 1 := by
    52	  have hkey : c * r + 1 ≤ 2 ^ (c * s + 1) := by
    53	    rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos c with hc | hc
    54	    · subst hc
    55	      simp
    56	    · obtain ⟨d, rfl⟩ : ∃ d, c = d + 1 := ⟨c - 1, by omega⟩
    57	      have h1 : d + 1 ≤ 2 ^ d := Nat.lt_two_pow_self
    58	      have h2 : (d + 1) * r ≤ 2 ^ d * 2 ^ s := Nat.mul_le_mul h1 hrs
    59	      have h3 : 1 ≤ 2 ^ d * 2 ^ s := by
    60	        have hp : 0 < 2 ^ d * 2 ^ s := by positivity
    61	        omega
    62	      have h4 : 2 ^ (d + 1 + s) = 2 ^ d * 2 ^ s + 2 ^ d * 2 ^ s := by
    63	        rw [pow_add, pow_succ]
    64	        ring
    65	      have h5 : d + 1 + s ≤ (d + 1) * s + 1 := by
    66	        have hds : d ≤ d * s := by
    67	          simpa using Nat.mul_le_mul (le_refl d) hs
    68	        have hexp : (d + 1) * s = d * s + s := by ring
    69	        omega
    70	      calc (d + 1) * r + 1 ≤ 2 ^ d * 2 ^ s + 2 ^ d * 2 ^ s :=
    71	            Nat.add_le_add h2 h3
    72	        _ = 2 ^ (d + 1 + s) := h4.symm
    73	        _ ≤ 2 ^ ((d + 1) * s + 1) := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) h5
    74	  calc Nat.log 2 (c * r + 1) ≤ Nat.log 2 (2 ^ (c * s + 1)) :=
    75	        Nat.log_mono_right hkey
    76	    _ = c * s + 1 := Nat.log_pow (by norm_num) _
    77	
    78	/-- The canonical tuple is admissible. This is the numerical
    79	admissibility part of `lem:delta-bound`, blueprint
    80	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:484-492`, paper
    81	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1520-1562`. -/
    82	theorem introParamsTuple_isAdmissible (a b : ℝ) (R : ℕ) (hR : 4 ≤ R) :
    83	    IsAdmissibleTuple (introParamsTuple (introParamsC a b) R) := by
    84	  have hEven : Even (introParamsC a b) := ⟨⌈(b + a) / (2 * b)⌉₊, two_mul _⟩

    35	-/
    36	def msConstraintVars (i : Fin 6) (j : Fin 3) : Fin 9 :=
    37	  ⟨if i.val < 3 then i.val * 3 + j.val else i.val - 3 + j.val * 3, by

    42	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    43	-/
    44	def msParity (i : Fin 6) : ZMod 2 :=
    45	  if i.val = 5 then 1 else 0

    48	`def:ms-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:207-222`, paper origin

# Mathematical Language Guidelines

MIPStarRE Lean names and documentation should be written for readers comparing
the formalization with the paper and blueprint.

This is a project-local supplement to the Mathlib-derived documentation,
naming, and style guides in the lean-conventions skill's `MATHLIB_doc`,
`MATHLIB_naming`, and `MATHLIB_style` references.

## Scope

These guidelines apply to:

- public Lean declaration names and namespace names;
- module docstrings;
- declaration docstrings;
- documentation-visible section comments;
- explanatory comments that describe the mathematical role of a declaration.
- blueprint prose and formalization-support notes;
- issue titles and issue bodies;
- PR titles and PR descriptions.

## Source of Truth

Use terminology from the following sources, in this order:

1. `references/ldt-paper/`
2. `blueprint/src/chapter/`
3. established local conventions in nearby Lean files

When the paper has a term for the object, use that term. For Section 5, for
example, prefer orthogonalization lemma, truncation function, rounding to
projectors, rank reduction, and completing to measurement.

## Reference Notation And Terminology

The notation and terminology of the original reference are the default for
reader-facing mathematical text.  A reader should be able to compare a Lean
docstring, blueprint paragraph, issue, or PR description with the cited source
without first learning a private vocabulary used by the formalization.

When Lean must use a different name or representation, define the deviation in a
location which future readers can find from the affected statement.  Use the
first applicable location in the following order:

1. the declaration docstring of the public object whose name or representation
   differs from the paper;
2. the module docstring of the defining Lean file, when the deviation concerns a
   family of declarations in that file;
3. the relevant blueprint paragraph, when the notation appears only in the
   blueprint;
4. a report under `docs/reports/` or `docs/paper-gaps/`, when the deviation is a
   larger discrepancy between the paper, blueprint, and Lean.

The explanation should say:

- the notation or term used in the paper;
- the Lean object or name which represents it;
- the mathematical reason for the difference, if there is one;
- the scope in which the replacement should be used.

A PR description may mention the deviation, but it should not be the only place
where future readers can learn it.

Formalization-only auxiliary lemmas should be introduced as such.  Their prose
should name the nearby paper equation, theorem, or construction they support,
rather than presenting the auxiliary name as paper terminology.

## Naming Norm

Names and prose should describe the mathematical object, hypothesis, or
conclusion. They should not encode the history of how the formalization was
assembled.

Avoid presenting words such as `pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`, `raw`,
`oneShot`, or `liveBlock` as mathematical terminology unless the cited source
uses them with that meaning. Likewise, avoid implementation-local substitutes
such as `projectivization` or `spectral truncation` when the paper gives a
clearer phrase.

This is a general rule for the repository, not only a rule for file splits.
Module names, namespace names, public declarations, theorem fields, docstrings,
blueprint-facing names, issue titles, and spec documents should name the
mathematical layer under discussion, not the local workflow step, paper line
number, or implementation history.

### Concrete examples

The table below illustrates the naming norm with examples patterned on the
codebase and on names seen during review.  Some entries are existing names;
others are proposed names for future refactors.  The "avoid" column lists
process-shaped names that encode the history of how the formalization was
assembled; the "prefer" column lists mathematical names that a reader of the
paper or blueprint would recognize.

| Avoid (process-shaped)                        | Prefer (mathematical)                     | Rationale                                              |
|:----------------------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------|
| `Line130`                                     | `ProjectiveConsistency`                   | Paper Lemma 5.13, not "the line-130 identity"          |
| `Line169`                                     | `CompletionTransport`                     | Paper Lemma 5.16, step that transports completed data  |
| `Step6`                                       | `Orthonormalization`                      | Paper Section 5, the orthonormalization construction   |
| `FinalAssembly`                               | `DiagonalCompletion`                      | Paper Lemma 5.17, constructing a diagonal POVM         |
| `OneShotIneq`                                 | `SelfConsistencyDataProcessing` (or existing module `Preliminaries.SelfConsistency.DataProcessing`)           | Paper's data-processing inequality for self-consistency |
| `PipelineCheck`                               | `ErrorPropagationBound` (proposed)                   | The bound that propagates error through the test       |
| `QxpLayerWrapper`                             | `ProjectivePOVMCompletion` (proposed)                | The construction from round-projectors to POVMs        |
| `RawSpectralTruncation`                       | `SpectralTruncation`                      | The paper's spectral truncation, not an "unwrapped" version |
| `AddInUStep3To5`                              | `AddInUUpperExcessMass` (proposed)                  | Paper Addendum in §U, the upper excess-mass estimate   |
| `AddInUStep12`                                | `AddInUCommutationTail` (proposed)                   | Paper Addendum in §U, the commutation tail estimate    |

An avoided name is acceptable only when the cited paper itself uses that
phrase as the mathematical name (e.g., a lemma the paper calls "Step 2").
In that case the docstring should cite the paper's phrasing.

File-split PRs are a common place where this rule matters: new leaves should be
named by the mathematical boundary they isolate, and any public declarations
exposed by the split should be reviewed under the same standard.

### Shared helpers

When the same (or nearly the same) helper declaration appears in two or
more chapter-local leaves, the copies should be consolidated into a single
shared helper in an appropriate common module.  This avoids duplication and
ensures that fixes, generalizations, or upstream replacements apply to all
call sites at once.  Issue [#1145] tracks this work across the repository.

Procedure:

1. **Confirm equivalence.**  Compare the statement of each copy.  If the
   types differ only by a chapter-specific parameterization (e.g.,
   `SubMeas (Polynomial params) ι` vs `SubMeas (Point params) ι`),
   parameterize the shared helper over that type via a `variable` or
   explicit argument.
2. **Find the right home.**  Prefer a module that is already imported by
   both call sites.  Typical candidates:
   - `MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic/` for parameter-free operators and bounds,
   - `MIPStarRE/LDT/Preliminaries/` for polynomial/field/character lemmas,
   - The highest chapter that is a common dependency of the two sites.
3. **Name mathematically.**  Give the shared helper a name that describes
   what it states, not which chapter it originally came from.
4. **Replace call sites.**  Delete the chapter-local copies and replace
   their uses with the shared helper.  A thin wrapper is allowed only when it
   preserves a paper-facing or blueprint-facing name that external readers
   need to search for; such wrappers should have a docstring or compatibility
   comment explaining why the alias exists.  Remove the wrapper once that
   paper-facing name is no longer needed for external reference.
5. **Document.**  Add a docstring to the shared helper citing the paper or
   blueprint location it supports.

### Legacy identifier treatment

If a docstring must mention a legacy Lean identifier, cite it in backticks and
describe the mathematical object in paper terminology. If an old public
identifier cannot be renamed in the current PR, record the required migration
in the issue, PR description, or an audit file under `audits/`.

Do not add an empty pass-through abbreviation merely to introduce a second
public name.  This is different from a documented public wrapper allowed in the
shared-helper procedure above: a wrapper must preserve a paper-facing or
blueprint-facing term and must say why the alias exists.

## Review Checklist

Reviewers should use this checklist when examining public names and
documentation prose.  Flag any item that fails.

- [ ] **Naming.**  Do public declaration names, namespace names, module names,
      theorem field names, and docstring prose describe a mathematical object,
      hypothesis, or conclusion?  Or do they encode the history of how the
      formalization was assembled (paper line numbers, workflow steps,
      implementation-phase labels)?
- [ ] **Source alignment.**  For the mathematical content under review, does
      the prose use the terminology in `references/ldt-paper/` or the
      blueprint?  Are process words such as `pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`,
      `raw`, `oneShot`, or `liveBlock` used as mathematical terms when the
      source does not use them that way?
- [ ] **Deviation documented.**  If a Lean name or representation differs from
      the paper, is the deviation documented in a declaration docstring,
      module docstring, blueprint paragraph, or `docs/paper-gaps/` note, in
      that order of preference?
- [ ] **Auxiliary lemmas.**  Are formalization-only auxiliary lemmas introduced
      as such, with prose naming the nearby paper equation, theorem, or
      construction they support?
- [ ] **Shared helpers.**  Does the PR introduce a helper that already exists
      (or near-exists) in another chapter-local leaf?  If so, has it been
      consolidated into a common module with a mathematical name?
- [ ] **Legacy IDs.**  If a legacy Lean identifier is mentioned, is the
      mathematical object described in paper terminology?  If an old public
      identifier cannot be renamed yet, is the required migration recorded in
      the issue, PR description, or an audit file?
- [ ] **Pass-through names.**  Does the PR add an empty pass-through
      abbreviation that introduces a second public name without adding
      mathematical content?  Reject it unless it is a documented compatibility
      wrapper preserving paper-facing or blueprint-facing terminology.

Review-fix PRs touching a surface covered by an active audit should read the
relevant audit before changing names or prose.

  1354			\begin{cases}

   132	\begin{definition}[Commuting and anticommuting tuples]
   133		\label{def:anticommuting-tuple}
   134		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliTuple}
   135		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.IsAnticommuting, MIPStarRE.QPBT.IsCommuting}
   136		\leanok
   137		% The quantity gamma is introduced in the source at eq:gamma-value, inside
   138		% the completeness analysis of the Pauli basis test; the definition below
   139		% is self-contained and does not depend on that occurrence.
   140		\uses{def:low-degree-encoding, def:subfield-trace}
   141		For a tuple
   142		$\omega = (u_X, u_Z, r_X, r_Z) \in (\F_q^m)^2 \times (\F_q)^2$, let
   143		\[
   144			\gamma(\omega) \,=\, \tr\big( (r_X \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u_X)) \cdot (r_Z \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u_Z)) \big)\,,
   145		\]
   146		where $r_W \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u_W)$ is the scalar multiple of the
   147		vector $\mathrm{ind}_m(u_W) \in \F_q^{M}$, the middle $\cdot$ is the
   148		$\F_q$-inner product of two vectors in $\F_q^{M}$, and
   149		$\tr = \tr_{q \to 2}$. The tuple $\omega$ is called \emph{anticommuting}
   150		if $\gamma(\omega) \neq 0$, and \emph{commuting} if $\gamma(\omega) = 0$.
   151	\end{definition}
   152	
   153	The sign $(-1)^{\gamma(\omega)}$ is exactly the sign with which the
   154	generalized Pauli observables $\tau^X(r_X \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u_X))$ and
   155	$\tau^Z(r_Z \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u_Z))$ commute
   156	(see Lemma~\ref{lem:twisted-commutation});
   157	this is the source of the terminology.
   158	
   159	\begin{lemma}[Probability of anticommuting tuples]
   160		\label{fact:omega-anticomm-prob}
   161		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.anticommProb, MIPStarRE.QPBT.anticommProb_eq}
   162		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.commProb, MIPStarRE.QPBT.commProb_ge_half}
   163		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.commProb_eq_one_sub_anticommProb}
   164		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.anticommProb_ge_of_m_le_q}
   165		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.anticommProb_ge_of_one_le_md}
   166		\leanok
   167		% The source states this result in a `fact' environment; it is stated here
   168		% as a lemma, and the paper label is kept verbatim.
   169		% The exact value of the anticommuting probability and the constant lower
   170		% bounds under the hypothesis m <= q are additions relative to the source,
   171		% which asserts only the two bounds displayed at the end of the statement;
   172		% the source states those bounds without the hypothesis m, d >= 1, under
   173		% which alone they hold (see the remark following this lemma). The
   174		% unconditional constant bounds are what the proof of the lemma labelled
   175		% lem:qld-win-implications uses.
   176		\uses{def:anticommuting-tuple}
   177		A tuple $\omega = (u_X,u_Z,r_X,r_Z)$ sampled uniformly at random from
   178		$(\F_q^m)^2 \times (\F_q)^2$ is anticommuting with probability exactly
   179		\[
   180			\big(1 - q^{-1}\big)^{m+1} \cdot \frac{1}{2}\,,
   181		\]
   182		and commuting with the complementary probability, which is at least
   183		$\frac12$. In particular, if $m \leq q$, then $\omega$ is anticommuting
   184		with probability at least $2^{-4}$ and commuting with probability at
   185		least $\frac12$. If $m, d \geq 1$, then the probability that $\omega$ is
   186		anticommuting is at least
   187		\[
   188			(1 - q^{-m}) \cdot (1 - q^{-1}) \cdot \Big(1 - \frac{md}{q}\Big) \cdot \frac{1}{2}
   189			\,\geq\, \Big(1 - \frac{3md}{q}\Big) \cdot \frac{1}{2}\,,
   190		\]
   191		and the probability that $\omega$ is commuting is also at least
   192		$\big(1 - \frac{3md}{q}\big) \cdot \frac{1}{2}$.
   193	\end{lemma}
   194	\begin{proof}
   195		\leanok
   196		\uses{def:low-degree-encoding, def:indicator-vector, def:admissible-size, def:binary-representation, lem:downsize_field, lem:one}
   197		By the definition of the indicator vector
   198		(Definition~\ref{def:indicator-vector}), expanding the product over the
   199		coordinates $i \in \{1, \dots, m\}$ into a sum over $y \in \{0,1\}^m$
   200		gives
   201		\[
   202			\mathrm{ind}_m(u_X) \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u_Z)
   203			\,=\, \sum_{y \in \{0,1\}^m} \mathrm{ind}_{m,y}(u_X)\, \mathrm{ind}_{m,y}(u_Z)
   204			\,=\, \prod_{i=1}^{m} \big( u_{X,i}\, u_{Z,i} + (1 - u_{X,i})(1 - u_{Z,i}) \big)\,,
   205		\]
   206		and since $\F_q$ has characteristic $2$, the $i$-th factor equals
   207		$1 + u_{X,i} + u_{Z,i}$. Hence
   208		\[
   209			\gamma(\omega) \,=\, \tr\Big( (r_X r_Z) \cdot \prod_{i=1}^{m} (1 + u_{X,i} + u_{Z,i}) \Big)\,.
   210		\]
   211		For any fixed $u_X$, the $m$ factors $1 + u_{X,i} + u_{Z,i}$ are
   212		independent and uniformly distributed in $\F_q$ over the choice of
   213		$u_Z$, so all of them are nonzero with probability $(1-q^{-1})^m$;

    32	space uses the once-and-for-all model `fixedFieldModel P.q P.hq`, rather than a
    33	model supplied by each parameter record.  This is the Lean carrier for
    34	`def:ld-game` in
    35	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-156`, with paper origin
    36	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.

    38	structure LdParams where
    39	  q : ℕ
    40	  m : ℕ
    41	  d : ℕ

   109	/-- The integer-coordinate map `χ` from the fixed field representation.  This
   110	is `eq:chi-func` in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   111	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`, paper origin
   112	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   113	-/
   114	noncomputable def chiIndex (P : LdParams) (s : ScalarQ P) : Fin P.m := by
   115	  letI : NeZero P.m := ⟨by
   116	    exact Nat.ne_of_gt (lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one P.hm)⟩
   117	  exact Fin.ofNat P.m ((binaryRepresentation P.model s).val / (P.q / P.m))
   118	
   119	/-- The projection used in the diagonal-line map zeroes coordinates before the
   120	chosen index and retains the suffix of the direction vector.  This is the
   121	prefix restriction in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   122	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`, paper origin
   123	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   124	-/
   125	def prefixProjection {P : LdParams} (i : Fin P.m) (v : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P) :
   126	    Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
   127	  fun j => if j.val < i.val then 0 else v j
   128	
   129	/-- The point CL map, retaining the point block and clearing the auxiliary
   130	blocks.  It is the map `L_point` of `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   131	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`, paper origin
   132	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   133	-/
   134	def ldPointCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   135	  fun i => match i with
   136	  | .inl (.inl j) => z (.inl (.inl j))
   137	  | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   138	  | .inr _ => 0
   139	
   140	/-- The affine-line CL map.  The direction block is put through the canonical
   141	line representative map from `def:line-representative`, while the point block
   142	is retained (blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`; paper
   143	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   144	-/
   145	noncomputable def ldALineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   146	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   147	  let rep := lineRepMap (coordinateDirection i)
   148	  fun i => match i with
   149	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   150	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   151	  | .inr _ => 0
   152	
   153	/-- The diagonal-line CL map, using the same canonical representative interface
   154	for the direction block.  This is the `L_DLine` clause of
   155	`def:ld-question-distribution` (blueprint
   156	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`; paper origin
   157	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   158	-/
   159	noncomputable def ldDLineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   160	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   161	  let direction := prefixProjection i (z.direction)
   162	  let rep := lineRepMap direction
   163	  fun i => match i with
   164	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   165	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   166	  | .inr j => direction j
   167	
   168	/-- Dispatch the three low-degree CL maps by question type.  This is the typed
   169	construction in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   170	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`, paper origin
   171	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   172	-/
   173	noncomputable def ldCL (P : LdParams) : LdType → LdSpace P → LdSpace P
   174	  | .point => ldPointCL P
   175	  | .aline => ldALineCL P
   176	  | .dline => ldDLineCL P

   179	coordinate of the ambient low-degree space.  It is the first register in the
   180	concatenation exhibiting the conditional-linearity levels asserted in

   563	noncomputable instance (P : LdParams) : Fintype (LdAnswer P) :=

   566	/-- Evaluation of a coefficient tuple at a field element.  This is the
   567	representative convention used by the line answers in `def:ld-win-predicate`,
   568	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:137-156`, paper origin
   569	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   570	-/
   571	def evalCoefficient {K : Type*} [Semiring K] {n : ℕ}
   572	    (c : Fin n → K) (t : K) : K :=
   573	  ∑ i : Fin n, c i * t ^ i.val
   574	
   575	/-- Check that an answer has the constructor prescribed by its question type;
   576	Lean encoding of the rejection clause in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   577	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:137-156`, paper origin
   578	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   579	-/
   580	def validLdAnswer {P : LdParams} (t : LdType) (a : LdAnswer P) : Bool :=
   581	  match t, a with
   582	  | .point, .pointVals _ => true
   583	  | .aline, .alinePolys _ => true
   584	  | .dline, .dlinePolys _ => true
   585	  | _, _ => false
   586	
   587	/-- The axis-parallel line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   588	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:137-156`, paper origin
   589	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   590	-/
   591	def alinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
   592	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   593	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   594	  -- Universal quantification follows the zero-direction convention in
   595	  -- `rem:ld-win-zero-direction`.
   596	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   597	    point.point = line.point + t • coordinateDirection (chiIndex P line.seed) →
   598	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   599	
   600	/-- The diagonal line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   601	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:137-156`, paper origin
   602	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   603	-/
   604	def dlinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
   605	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   606	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   607	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   608	    point.point = line.point + t • line.direction →
   609	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   610	
   611	/-- The low-degree consistency predicate, rejecting answers of the wrong
   612	constructor shape.  This is `def:ld-win-predicate` in
   613	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:137-156`, paper origin
   614	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   615	-/
   616	noncomputable def ldWinPredicate (P : LdParams) :
   617	    LdQuestion P → LdQuestion P → LdAnswer P → LdAnswer P → Bool :=
   618	  open Classical in
   619	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   620	      if validLdAnswer tA a && validLdAnswer tB b then
   621	        match tA, tB, a, b with
   622	        | .point, .point, .pointVals u, .pointVals v => decide (u = v)
   623	        | .aline, .point, .alinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   624	            decide (alinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   625	        | .point, .aline, .pointVals u, .alinePolys f =>
   626	            decide (alinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   627	        | .dline, .point, .dlinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   628	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   629	        | .point, .dline, .pointVals u, .dlinePolys f =>
   630	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   631	        | .aline, .aline, .alinePolys f, .alinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   632	        | .dline, .dline, .dlinePolys f, .dlinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   633	        | _, _, _, _ => true
   634	      else false
   635	
   636	/-- The low-degree game packaged as a `Game`.  This is `def:ld-game` in
   637	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-156`, paper origin
   638	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   639	-/
   640	noncomputable def ldGame (P : LdParams) : Game where
   641	  QuestionA := LdQuestion P
   642	  QuestionB := LdQuestion P
   643	  AnswerA := LdAnswer P
   644	  AnswerB := LdAnswer P
   645	  μ := ldQuestionDistribution P
   646	  μ_prob := by
   647	    exact Distribution.IsProbability.map
   648	      (uniformDistribution_isProbability ((LdType × LdType) × LdSpace P)) _
   649	  decide := ldWinPredicate P
   650	
   651	end

    36	/-- The smallest even natural number represented by the ceiling prescription
    37	in `def:introparams`. -/
    38	noncomputable def introParamsC (a b : ℝ) : ℕ :=
    39	  2 * ⌈(b + a) / (2 * b)⌉₊
    40	
    41	/-- The canonical `(q, m, d)` tuple of `def:introparams`. -/
    42	def introParamsTuple (c R : ℕ) : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ :=
    43	  (2 ^ (c * Nat.clog 2 (Nat.clog 2 R) + 1),
    44	    2 ^ Nat.log 2 (c * Nat.clog 2 R + 1), 1)
    45	
    46	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: a numerical comparison of the two exponents
    47	appearing in the canonical tuple.  If `s` is positive and `r` is at most
    48	`2 ^ s`, then the base-two logarithm of `c * r + 1` does not exceed
    49	`c * s + 1`. -/
    50	private theorem log_two_le_mul_add_one (c r s : ℕ) (hs : 1 ≤ s)
    51	    (hrs : r ≤ 2 ^ s) : Nat.log 2 (c * r + 1) ≤ c * s + 1 := by
    52	  have hkey : c * r + 1 ≤ 2 ^ (c * s + 1) := by
    53	    rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos c with hc | hc
    54	    · subst hc
    55	      simp
    56	    · obtain ⟨d, rfl⟩ : ∃ d, c = d + 1 := ⟨c - 1, by omega⟩
    57	      have h1 : d + 1 ≤ 2 ^ d := Nat.lt_two_pow_self
    58	      have h2 : (d + 1) * r ≤ 2 ^ d * 2 ^ s := Nat.mul_le_mul h1 hrs
    59	      have h3 : 1 ≤ 2 ^ d * 2 ^ s := by
    60	        have hp : 0 < 2 ^ d * 2 ^ s := by positivity
    61	        omega
    62	      have h4 : 2 ^ (d + 1 + s) = 2 ^ d * 2 ^ s + 2 ^ d * 2 ^ s := by
    63	        rw [pow_add, pow_succ]
    64	        ring
    65	      have h5 : d + 1 + s ≤ (d + 1) * s + 1 := by
    66	        have hds : d ≤ d * s := by
    67	          simpa using Nat.mul_le_mul (le_refl d) hs
    68	        have hexp : (d + 1) * s = d * s + s := by ring
    69	        omega
    70	      calc (d + 1) * r + 1 ≤ 2 ^ d * 2 ^ s + 2 ^ d * 2 ^ s :=
    71	            Nat.add_le_add h2 h3
    72	        _ = 2 ^ (d + 1 + s) := h4.symm
    73	        _ ≤ 2 ^ ((d + 1) * s + 1) := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) h5
    74	  calc Nat.log 2 (c * r + 1) ≤ Nat.log 2 (2 ^ (c * s + 1)) :=
    75	        Nat.log_mono_right hkey
    76	    _ = c * s + 1 := Nat.log_pow (by norm_num) _
    77	
    78	/-- The canonical tuple is admissible. This is the numerical
    79	admissibility part of `lem:delta-bound`, blueprint
    80	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:484-492`, paper
    81	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1520-1562`. -/
    82	theorem introParamsTuple_isAdmissible (a b : ℝ) (R : ℕ) (hR : 4 ≤ R) :
    83	    IsAdmissibleTuple (introParamsTuple (introParamsC a b) R) := by
    84	  have hEven : Even (introParamsC a b) := ⟨⌈(b + a) / (2 * b)⌉₊, two_mul _⟩
    85	  have hpow : Nat.clog 2 (2 ^ 2) ≤ Nat.clog 2 R :=
    86	    Nat.clog_mono_right 2 (by simpa using hR)
    87	  have hr2 : 2 ≤ Nat.clog 2 R := by
    88	    rwa [Nat.clog_pow 2 2 (by norm_num)] at hpow
    89	  have hs1 : 1 ≤ Nat.clog 2 (Nat.clog 2 R) := Nat.clog_pos (by norm_num) hr2
    90	  have hrs : Nat.clog 2 R ≤ 2 ^ Nat.clog 2 (Nat.clog 2 R) :=
    91	    Nat.le_pow_clog (by norm_num) _
    92	  exact ⟨⟨introParamsC a b * Nat.clog 2 (Nat.clog 2 R) + 1,
    93	      (hEven.mul_right _).add_one, rfl⟩,
    94	    Nat.one_le_pow _ _ (by norm_num), le_rfl,
    95	    pow_dvd_pow 2 (log_two_le_mul_add_one _ _ _ hs1 hrs)⟩
    96	
    97	/-- The canonical admissible parameter structure of `def:introparams`,
    98	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:471-482`, paper
    99	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1503-1514`. -/
   100	noncomputable def introParams (a b : ℝ) (R : ℕ) (hR : 4 ≤ R) :
   101	    AdmissibleParams :=
   102	  AdmissibleParams.ofTuple _ (introParamsTuple_isAdmissible a b R hR)
   103	
   104	/-- The canonical parameter dimension supplies at least `R` encoded
   105	coordinates, as asserted in `lem:delta-bound`. -/
   106	theorem le_two_pow_introParams_m (a b : ℝ) (ha : 1 ≤ a) (hb : 0 < b)
   107	    (R : ℕ) (hR : 4 ≤ R) :
   108	    R ≤ 2 ^ (introParams a b R hR).m := by
   109	  have hc2 : 2 ≤ introParamsC a b := by
   110	    have hceil : 0 < ⌈(b + a) / (2 * b)⌉₊ :=
   111	      Nat.ceil_pos.mpr (div_pos (by linarith) (by linarith))
   112	    show 2 ≤ 2 * ⌈(b + a) / (2 * b)⌉₊
   113	    omega
   114	  have hlt : introParamsC a b * Nat.clog 2 R + 1 <
   115	      2 ^ Nat.log 2 (introParamsC a b * Nat.clog 2 R + 1) * 2 := by
   116	    simpa [pow_succ] using
   117	      Nat.lt_pow_succ_log_self (b := 2) (by norm_num)
   118	        (introParamsC a b * Nat.clog 2 R + 1)
   119	  have hmul : 2 * Nat.clog 2 R ≤ introParamsC a b * Nat.clog 2 R :=
   120	    Nat.mul_le_mul hc2 (le_refl _)
   121	  have key : Nat.clog 2 R ≤
   122	      2 ^ Nat.log 2 (introParamsC a b * Nat.clog 2 R + 1) := by
   123	    omega
   124	  calc R ≤ 2 ^ Nat.clog 2 R := Nat.le_pow_clog (by norm_num) R
   125	    _ ≤ 2 ^ (2 ^ Nat.log 2 (introParamsC a b * Nat.clog 2 R + 1)) :=
   126	        Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) key
   127	    _ = 2 ^ (introParams a b R hR).m := rfl

   129	/-- `lem:delta-bound`: the Pauli soundness error at the canonical parameters
   130	has polylogarithmic dependence on `R`. Blueprint
   131	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:484-492`, paper
   132	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1520-1562`.

   134	The explicit nonnegativity premise records the failure-probability domain
   135	inherited from `thm:pauli`; fractional powers of a negative real do not express
   136	the source's error parameter.
   137	
   138	**Local fix:** The third error term is bounded directly using the lower bound
   139	on `m`, rather than the source's false intermediate comparison between the
   140	field exponent and `m`. This discrepancy is documented in issue #16 and
   141	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_delta-bound-exponent-comparison.tex`; see also
   142	`rem:delta-bound-exponent-comparison`. -/
   143	theorem exists_deltaQld_introParams_bound (a b : ℝ) (ha : 1 ≤ a)
   144	    (hb : 0 < b) (hb' : b < 1) :
   145	    ∃ a' b' : ℝ, 1 ≤ a' ∧ 0 < b' ∧ b' ≤ 1 ∧
   146	      ∀ (R : ℕ) (hR : 4 ≤ R) (ε : ℝ),

    18	/-- The product of two finite distributions, a formalization-only auxiliary
    19	used by the sandwich construction; blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:427-454`,
    20	paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:465-501`. -/
    21	noncomputable def Distribution.prod {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    22	    (μ : Distribution α) (ν : Distribution β) : Distribution (α × β) where
    23	  support := μ.support.product ν.support
    24	  weight p := μ.weight p.1 * ν.weight p.2
    25	  nonnegative p := mul_nonneg (μ.nonnegative p.1) (ν.nonnegative p.2)
    26	  outsideSupport p hp := by
    27	    by_cases hμ : p.1 ∈ μ.support
    28	    · have hν : p.2 ∉ ν.support := by
    29	        intro h
    30	        exact hp (Finset.mem_product.mpr ⟨hμ, h⟩)
    31	      simp [ν.outsideSupport p.2 hν]
    32	    · simp [μ.outsideSupport p.1 hμ]

    34	/-- The product of two probability distributions is a probability
    35	distribution; blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:427-454`, paper
    36	`06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:465-501`. -/
    37	theorem Distribution.prod_isProbability {α β : Type*}
    38	    [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β] (μ : Distribution α) (ν : Distribution β)
    39	    (hμ : μ.IsProbability) (hν : ν.IsProbability) :
    40	    (Distribution.prod μ ν).IsProbability := by
    41	  simp only [Distribution.IsProbability, Distribution.totalWeight,
    42	    Distribution.prod]
    43	  calc
    44	    (∑ p ∈ μ.support.product ν.support, μ.weight p.1 * ν.weight p.2) =
    45	        ∑ a ∈ μ.support, ∑ b ∈ ν.support, μ.weight a * ν.weight b := by
    46	      exact Finset.sum_product' μ.support ν.support
    47	        (fun a b => μ.weight a * ν.weight b)
    48	    _ =
    49	        ∑ a ∈ μ.support, μ.weight a * ∑ b ∈ ν.support, ν.weight b := by
    50	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    51	      intro a _
    52	      exact (Finset.mul_sum ν.support (fun b => ν.weight b) (μ.weight a)).symm
    53	    _ = ∑ a ∈ μ.support, μ.weight a := by
    54	      rw [hν.weight_sum_eq_one]
    55	      simp
    56	    _ = 1 := hμ.weight_sum_eq_one
    57	
    58	/-- The convex mixture with a coefficient in `[0,1]`, as used for
    59	the equal mixture in `def:line-point-dist`, blueprint
    60	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:125-135`, paper
    61	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:274-287`. -/
    62	noncomputable def Distribution.mix {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α]
    63	    (t : ℝ) (ht0 : 0 ≤ t) (ht1 : t ≤ 1)
    64	    (μ ν : Distribution α) : Distribution α where
    65	  support := μ.support ∪ ν.support
    66	  weight a := t * μ.weight a + (1 - t) * ν.weight a
    67	  nonnegative a := by
    68	    exact add_nonneg
    69	      (mul_nonneg ht0 (μ.nonnegative a))
    70	      (mul_nonneg (sub_nonneg.mpr ht1) (ν.nonnegative a))
    71	  outsideSupport a ha := by
    72	    have hμ : a ∉ μ.support := fun h => ha (Finset.mem_union_left _ h)
    73	    have hν : a ∉ ν.support := fun h => ha (Finset.mem_union_right _ h)
    74	    simp [μ.outsideSupport a hμ, ν.outsideSupport a hν]
    75	
    76	/-- A convex mixture of probability distributions is a probability distribution;
    77	`def:line-point-dist`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:125-135`, paper
    78	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:274-287`. -/
    79	theorem Distribution.mix_isProbability {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α]
    80	    (t : ℝ) (μ ν : Distribution α) (hμ : μ.IsProbability)
    81	    (hν : ν.IsProbability) (ht0 : 0 ≤ t) (ht1 : t ≤ 1) :
    82	    (Distribution.mix t ht0 ht1 μ ν).IsProbability := by
    83	  have hμ_union :
    84	      ∑ a ∈ μ.support ∪ ν.support, μ.weight a = 1 := by
    85	    apply hμ.weight_sum_eq_one_of_subset
    86	    intro a ha
    87	    exact Finset.mem_union_left ν.support ha
    88	  have hν_union :
    89	      ∑ a ∈ μ.support ∪ ν.support, ν.weight a = 1 := by
    90	    apply hν.weight_sum_eq_one_of_subset
    91	    intro a ha
    92	    exact Finset.mem_union_right μ.support ha
    93	  simp only [Distribution.IsProbability, Distribution.totalWeight,
    94	    Distribution.mix]
    95	  rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib, ← Finset.mul_sum, ← Finset.mul_sum,
    96	    hμ_union, hν_union]
    97	  ring

    99	/-- The dependent bind of finite distributions used for typed question
   100	distributions, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1268-1272`, paper
   101	`07_types.tex:84-94`. -/
   102	noncomputable def Distribution.bind {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
   103	    (μ : Distribution α) (ν : α → Distribution β) : Distribution β where
   104	  support := μ.support.biUnion (fun a => (ν a).support)
   105	  weight b := ∑ a ∈ μ.support, μ.weight a * (ν a).weight b
   106	  nonnegative b := Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => mul_nonneg (μ.nonnegative a) ((ν a).nonnegative b)
   107	  outsideSupport b hb := by
   108	    apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
   109	    intro a ha
   110	    have hnot : b ∉ (ν a).support := by
   111	      intro h
   112	      exact hb (Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr ⟨a, ha, h⟩)
   113	    simp [ν a |>.outsideSupport b hnot]

   115	/-- A dependent bind of probability distributions is a probability distribution;
   116	blueprint
   117	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1268-1272`, paper `07_types.tex:84-94`. -/
   118	theorem Distribution.bind_isProbability {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
   119	    (μ : Distribution α) (ν : α → Distribution β) (hμ : μ.IsProbability)
   120	    (hν : ∀ a ∈ μ.support, (ν a).IsProbability) :
   121	    (Distribution.bind μ ν).IsProbability := by
   122	  classical
   123	  have hν_union (a : α) (ha : a ∈ μ.support) :
   124	      ∑ b ∈ μ.support.biUnion (fun a => (ν a).support), (ν a).weight b = 1 := by
   125	    apply (hν a ha).weight_sum_eq_one_of_subset
   126	    intro b hb
   127	    exact Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr ⟨a, ha, hb⟩
   128	  simp only [Distribution.IsProbability, Distribution.totalWeight,
   129	    Distribution.bind]
   130	  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   131	  calc
   132	    (∑ a ∈ μ.support,
   133	        ∑ b ∈ μ.support.biUnion (fun a => (ν a).support),
   134	          μ.weight a * (ν a).weight b) =
   135	        ∑ a ∈ μ.support,
   136	          μ.weight a *
   137	            ∑ b ∈ μ.support.biUnion (fun a => (ν a).support),
   138	              (ν a).weight b := by
   139	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   140	      intro a _
   141	      exact (Finset.mul_sum _ (fun b => (ν a).weight b) (μ.weight a)).symm
   142	    _ = ∑ a ∈ μ.support, μ.weight a := by
   143	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   144	      intro a ha
   145	      rw [hν_union a ha]
   146	      simp
   147	    _ = 1 := hμ.weight_sum_eq_one

   149	/-- Restrict a distribution to a decidable positive-mass event and normalize it,
   150	as in `def:ith-restricted-line`; blueprint
   151	`ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:600-618`, paper
   152	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1038-1048`. -/
   153	noncomputable def Distribution.restrict {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α]
   154	    (μ : Distribution α) (p : α → Prop) [DecidablePred p]
   155	    (hpos : 0 < ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter p, μ.weight a) : Distribution α where
   156	  support := μ.support.filter p
   157	  weight a := if p a then μ.weight a / ∑ b ∈ μ.support.filter p, μ.weight b else 0
   158	  nonnegative a := by
   159	    split
   160	    · exact div_nonneg (μ.nonnegative a) (le_of_lt hpos)
   161	    · exact le_rfl
   162	  outsideSupport a ha := by
   163	    by_cases hp : p a
   164	    · have hμ : a ∉ μ.support := fun h => ha (Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨h, hp⟩)
   165	      simp [hp, μ.outsideSupport a hμ]
   166	    · simp [hp]
   167	
   168	/-- Restriction to a positive-mass event preserves total probability;
   169	`def:ith-restricted-line`, blueprint
   170	`ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:600-618`, paper
   171	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1038-1048`. -/
   172	theorem Distribution.restrict_isProbability {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α]
   173	    (μ : Distribution α) (p : α → Prop) [DecidablePred p]
   174	    (hpos : 0 < ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter p, μ.weight a) :
   175	    (Distribution.restrict μ p hpos).IsProbability := by
   176	  simp only [Distribution.IsProbability, Distribution.totalWeight,
   177	    Distribution.restrict]
   178	  calc
   179	    (∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter p,
   180	        if p a then μ.weight a / ∑ b ∈ μ.support.filter p, μ.weight b else 0) =
   181	        ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter p,
   182	          μ.weight a / ∑ b ∈ μ.support.filter p, μ.weight b := by
   183	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   184	      intro a ha
   185	      rw [if_pos (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha).2]
   186	    _ = (∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter p, μ.weight a) /
   187	        ∑ b ∈ μ.support.filter p, μ.weight b := by
   188	      rw [Finset.sum_div]
   189	    _ = 1 := div_self hpos.ne'

+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: over a commutative ring of characteristic
+    [CharP K 2] {m : ℕ} (x z : Fin m → K) :
+    ∑ y : Cube m, indicatorVec x y * indicatorVec z y
+      = ∏ i : Fin m, (1 + x i + z i) := by
+  have h2 : (2 : K) = 0 := CharTwo.two_eq_zero
+  have hev : ∀ (u : Fin m → K) (y : Cube m),
+      indicatorVec u y = ∏ i : Fin m, if y i then u i else 1 - u i := by
+    intro u y
+    simp [indicatorVec, indicatorPoly, apply_ite]
+  have hfac : ∀ i : Fin m,
+      ∑ b : Bool, ((if b then x i else 1 - x i) * (if b then z i else 1 - z i))
+        = 1 + x i + z i := by
+    intro i
+    have h1 :
+        ∑ b : Bool, ((if b then x i else 1 - x i) * (if b then z i else 1 - z i))
+          = x i * z i + (1 - x i) * (1 - z i) := by
+      rw [Fintype.sum_bool]
+      simp
+    rw [h1]
+    linear_combination (x i * z i - x i - z i) * h2
+  calc ∑ y : Cube m, indicatorVec x y * indicatorVec z y
+      = ∑ y : Cube m, ∏ i : Fin m,
+          ((if y i then x i else 1 - x i) * (if y i then z i else 1 - z i)) := by
+        refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
+        intro y _
+        rw [hev x y, hev z y, ← Finset.prod_mul_distrib]
+    _ = ∏ i : Fin m, ∑ b : Bool,
+          ((if b then x i else 1 - x i) * (if b then z i else 1 - z i)) := by
+        rw [Finset.prod_univ_sum, Fintype.piFinset_univ]
+    _ = ∏ i : Fin m, (1 + x i + z i) := Finset.prod_congr rfl fun i _ => hfac i

+  haveI := pauliScalar_charTwo P
+  have hprod : (∑ y : Cube P.m, indicatorVec uX y * indicatorVec uZ y)
+      = ∏ i : Fin P.m, (1 + uX i + uZ i) :=

+  congr 1
+  rw [← hprod]
+  simp only [dotProduct, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, Finset.mul_sum]
+  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun y _ => by ring

+    2 * (Finset.univ.filter

+  haveI := pauliScalar_charTwo P
+  have hK := card_pauliScalar P

+    refine ⟨P.model.basis ⟨0, hpos⟩ * P.model.basis ⟨0, hpos⟩, ?_⟩
+    simpa [fixedBinTrace, binTrace] using P.model.selfDual ⟨0, hpos⟩ ⟨0, hpos⟩

+  have himg :
+      (Finset.univ.filter
+          (fun a : PauliScalar P => fixedBinTrace P.model a = 0)).image (fun a => a + b)
+        = Finset.univ.filter
+            (fun a : PauliScalar P => ¬ (fixedBinTrace P.model a = 0)) := by
+    ext a
+    simp only [Finset.mem_image, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
+    constructor
+    · rintro ⟨c, hc, rfl⟩
+      rw [hadd, hc, hb]
+      simp
+    · intro ha
+      refine ⟨a + b, ?_, ?_⟩
+      · rw [hadd, hb]
+        have hone : fixedBinTrace P.model a = 1 := by
+          revert ha
+          generalize fixedBinTrace P.model a = t
+          revert t
+          decide
+        rw [hone]
+        decide

+    fun _ _ h => by simpa using h

+      (Finset.univ.filter (fun a : PauliScalar P => fixedBinTrace P.model a = 0)).card
+        = (Finset.univ.filter
+            (fun a : PauliScalar P => ¬ (fixedBinTrace P.model a = 0))).card := by
+    rw [← himg, Finset.card_image_of_injective _ hinj]

+      (Finset.univ.filter (fun a : PauliScalar P => fixedBinTrace P.model a = 0)).card
+          + (Finset.univ.filter
+              (fun a : PauliScalar P => ¬ (fixedBinTrace P.model a = 0))).card
+        = Fintype.card (PauliScalar P) :=
+    Finset.card_filter_add_card_filter_not _

+  simp only [ne_eq]
+  omega

+      = P.q ^ (P.m + 1) * (P.q - 1) ^ (P.m + 1) := by

+  have h2 : (2 : PauliScalar P) = 0 := CharTwo.two_eq_zero

+  have hN : 2 * N = P.q := two_mul_card_trace_ne P
+  -- the innermost sum, over the second scalar coordinate
+  have hinner : ∀ c : PauliScalar P,
+      (∑ r : PauliScalar P, if fixedBinTrace P.model (r * c) ≠ 0 then (1 : ℕ) else 0)
+        = if c = 0 then 0 else N := by
+    intro c
+    by_cases hc : c = 0
+    · subst hc
+      simp [htr0]
+    · rw [if_neg hc, hNdef, Finset.card_filter]
+      exact Fintype.sum_equiv (Equiv.mulRight₀ c hc)
+        (fun r => if fixedBinTrace P.model (r * c) ≠ 0 then (1 : ℕ) else 0)
+        (fun a => if fixedBinTrace P.model a ≠ 0 then (1 : ℕ) else 0)
+        (fun r => rfl)
+  -- the sum over the first scalar coordinate
+  have hnzcard :
+      (Finset.univ.filter (fun x : PauliScalar P => ¬ (x = 0))).card = P.q - 1 := by
+    have h1 : (Finset.univ.filter (fun x : PauliScalar P => x ≠ 0))
+        = Finset.univ.erase 0 := Finset.filter_ne' _ _
+    simp only [ne_eq] at h1
+    rw [h1, Finset.card_erase_of_mem (Finset.mem_univ _), Finset.card_univ, hK]
+  have hmid : ∀ dd : PauliScalar P,
+      (∑ rX : PauliScalar P, if rX * dd = 0 then (0 : ℕ) else N)
+        = if dd = 0 then 0 else (P.q - 1) * N := by
+    intro dd
+    by_cases hd : dd = 0
+    · subst hd
+      simp
+    · rw [if_neg hd]
+      have hcong : ∀ rX : PauliScalar P,
+          (if rX * dd = 0 then (0 : ℕ) else N) = if rX = 0 then 0 else N := by
+        intro rX
+        by_cases hr : rX = 0
+        · simp [hr]
+        · rw [if_neg (by simpa using mul_ne_zero hr hd), if_neg hr]
+      rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun x _ => hcong x), Finset.sum_ite]
+      simp [hnzcard]

+    intro uX
+    have hset : (Finset.univ.filter (fun uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P =>

+      ext uZ
+      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, Fintype.mem_piFinset,

+        linear_combination (1 + uX i) * h2

+    simp [Finset.card_erase_of_mem, Finset.card_univ, hK]

+      (∑ uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P,

+        rw [gammaValue_eq_trace_prod]

+      = P.q ^ P.m * ((P.q - 1) ^ P.m * ((P.q - 1) * N)) := by
+    rw [Finset.card_filter]
+    simp only [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
+    calc (∑ uX : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P, ∑ uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P,

+  rw [hexpand, hN, pow_succ, pow_succ]
+  ring

+private theorem clReindexTerm_supportedOn {K κ ι : Type*} [Field K]
+    [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {f : κ → ι}
+    (hf : Function.Injective f) :
+    ∀ {ell : ℕ} (t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := κ) ell) (S : Finset κ)
+      (T : Finset ι), t.supportedOn S → S.image f ⊆ T →
+      (clReindexTerm hf t).supportedOn T := by

+  induction t with
+  | zero => intro S T _ _; trivial
+  | succ S₁ L₁ hL rest ih =>
+      intro S T hsupp hST
+      obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := hsupp
+      refine ⟨fun i hi => hST (Finset.image_subset_image h1 hi), fun y => ?_⟩
+      refine ih (fun k => y (f k)) (S \ S₁) (T \ S₁.image f) (h2 _) ?_
+      intro i hi
+      obtain ⟨k, hk, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hi
+      obtain ⟨hkS, hkS₁⟩ := Finset.mem_sdiff.mp hk
+      refine Finset.mem_sdiff.mpr ⟨hST (Finset.mem_image_of_mem f hkS), ?_⟩
+      intro hmem
+      obtain ⟨k', hk', hk'eq⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hmem
+      exact hkS₁ (hf hk'eq ▸ hk')

+    ∀ {ell : ℕ} (t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := κ) ell) (x : ι → K),

+  intro ell t
+  induction t with

+  | succ S₁ L₁ hL rest ih =>

+          coordinateRestriction S₁ (fun k => x (f k)) := by
+        funext k

+        · have hmem : f k ∈ S₁.image f := Finset.mem_image_of_mem f hk

+        · have hni : f k ∉ S₁.image f := by
+            intro hmem

+            (coordinateRestriction (S₁.image f) x) (f k)) =
+          L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ (fun k => x (f k))) := by
+        rw [hhead]
+        exact clExtend_comp hf _

+          CondLinearTerm.eval (clReindexTerm hf (rest
+            (fun k => clReindexLinear hf L₁
+              (coordinateRestriction (S₁.image f) x) (f k)))) x =
+        clExtend f (L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ (fun k => x (f k))) +
+          CondLinearTerm.eval

   965	We now describe the question distribution of the game $\game^\pauli$, and show

  1073	\paragraph{Conditional linear functions for the Pauli basis test.}
  1074	The CL functions corresponding to the Pauli basis test question distribution are
  1075	parameterized by the parameter tuple $\qldparams = (q,m,d)$.
  1076	Let $V^\pauli$ denote the linear space $(\F_q^m)^2 \times \F_q \times \F_q^m
  1077	\times (\F_q)^2$.
  1078	The space $V^\pauli$ is decomposed into a direct sum of the following register
  1079	subspaces: $V_\xpt,V_\zpt$ (which are $m$-dimensional), $V_\coord$ (which is
  1080	$1$-dimensional), $V_{\dir{}}$ (which is $m$-dimensional), and
  1081	$V_{\rxpt},V_{\rzpt}$ (which are $1$-dimensional).
  1082	We identify elements of $V^\pauli$ as tuples $(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1083	\in (\F_q^m)^2 \times \F_q \times \F_q^m \times (\F_q)^2$.
  1084	We define CL functions $L_\tvar: V^\pauli \to V^\pauli$ for every type $\tvar
  1085	\in \type^\pauli$:
  1086	\begin{enumerate}
  1087	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\Point,W}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1088	  = L_\Point(u_W,s,v)$ where $L_\Point$ is the $1$-level CL function defined in
  1089	  \Cref{eq:cl-ptf}.\footnote{The range $V_{\xpt} \oplus V_\coord \oplus
  1090	    V_{\dir{}}$ or $V_{\zpt} \oplus V_\coord \oplus V_{\dir{}}$ of $L_\Point$ is
  1091	    embedded in $V^\pauli$ in the natural way.
  1092	    The same convention is used also in Item 2 and 3 for $L_\ALine$ and
  1093	    $L_\DLine$.}
  1094	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\ALine,W}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1095	  = L_\ALine(u_W,s,v)$ where $L_\ALine$ is the $2$-level CL function defined in
  1096	  \Cref{eq:cl-alnf}.
  1097	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\DLine,W}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1098	  = L_\DLine(u_W,s,v)$ where $L_\DLine$ is the $3$-level CL function defined in
  1099	  \Cref{eq:cl-dlnf}.
  1100	\item For $\tvar \in \type^\ms \cup \{\Pair, (\Pair,X), (\Pair,Z) \}$,
  1101	  $L_{\tvar}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt) =
  1102	  (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,0,0,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)$, i.e., it projects onto $V_\xpt \oplus
  1103	  V_\zpt \oplus V_{\rxpt} \oplus V_{\rzpt}$.
  1104	  Thus $L_{\tvar}$ is a $1$-level CL function.
  1105	  
  1106	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\Pauli,W} = 0$ as the identically $0$
  1107	  function.
  1108	  Thus it is a $0$-level CL function.
  1109	
  1110	\end{enumerate}
  1111	We note that the maps $L_{\Point,W}, L_{\ALine,W}, L_{\DLine,W}$ act as the zero function
  1112	on $V_{\overline{W}} \oplus V_{\rxpt} \oplus V_{\rzpt}$ where $\overline{W} = X$
  1113	if $W = Z$ and $\overline{W} = Z$ if $W = X$.
  1114	
  1115	The question distribution of $\game^\pauli$ is thus a typed CL distribution on
  1116	$\type^\pauli \times V^\pauli \times \type^\pauli \times V^\pauli$ where
  1117	$(\tvar_\alice,x_\alice,\tvar_\bob,x_\bob)$ is sampled by first uniformly
  1118	sampling an edge $(\tvar_\alice,\tvar_\bob)$ from the graph $G^\pauli$ defined
  1119	in Figure~\ref{fig:type-graph-pauli}, sampling a uniformly random $z \in
  1120	V^\pauli$, and then setting $x_w = L_{\tvar_w}(z)$ for $w \in \AB$.
